sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Associated Coaters is a small Kolkata architectural/industrial metal-coating and powder business, a capacity-utilization/value watchlist rather than an evidence-backed compounder. Sales expanded strongly, but recurring EBIT and recent cash conversion lagged the capital committed. At the secondary October 16 close of ₹96.50, the funded base case returns 11.69% annually versus a 15% hurdle, with substantial execution illiquidity. BQS 5.0/GQS 5.9/IAS 4.3 indicate weak assessed setup, not a trade instruction. Better collections, operating returns and control evidence matter more than another capacity announcement. [S1–S9]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff: 20 October 2026, IST economic reporting dates; last market session 19 October, but latest observed BSE trade 16 October at ₹96.50. Identity Associated Coaters Limited, BSE 544183/ASSOCIATED, ISIN INE0RIQ01013; listing 6 June 2024. Standalone Indian GAAP, ₹ crore; 1,352,000 issued shares imply ₹13.0468 crore market value. Five-year nominal pretax equity horizon/hurdle 15%; illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is not an allocation. All four gates are Conditional, with no evidenced G1/G3 failure. Historical financial/growth/valuation-input confidence Medium after primary restated/annual reconciliation; controls Medium with specific caveats. Forecast uncertainty remains high and separate. [S1–S7,S9]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors: GOV4, MOAT4, REV8, DUR5, CAP4, CASH5, BAL7, EXEC5, EARN4; R4/D5/P5/L1. Exact BQS 5.00, GQS 5.90, IAS 4.25 (displayed 4.3), each 100% covered with no discretionary cap. REV starting 9 from three-year 32.04% CAGR is capped 8 for Medium subject confidence and short relevant history, not small market size. Moving GOV and CAP one point each changes BQS by±0.32 and IAS by±0.08; changing R and D one point each changes IAS±0.55. These judgment differences exceed nearby ranking gaps. Methodology is a research convention, not a validated return predictor.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Pretreatment and powder/PVDF/wood-finish coating is sold to architectural, aluminium-extrusion and industrial clients; the company is adding in-house powder manufacturing. Receipts depend on customers completing their own projects, while significant related premises and labour links remain. The listed company was incorporated 2017 but FY2021 had zero revenue and operations scaled after promoter-asset transfer; the brochure’s family-business history from 1984 is not a 40-year listed-company cash record. No subsidiary/NCI perimeter applies. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Approved-applicator status and process breadth can reduce customer qualification effort, but do not establish exclusivity or pricing power. The prospectus says no suitably comparable listed peer exists given nature and scale; forcing paint-formulator multiples would mislead. Asian Paints, AkzoNobel and Jotun are named coating-system relationships, not equal service-company valuation peers, and no supplier premium is imported. Historical top-five concentration 78.89% at December 2023, regional competition and FY26 materials growth 77.75% versus sales 38.69% are contrary evidence. Named customer percentages are historical, not a current concentration estimate. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Primary six-observation revenue sequence FY2021–FY2026 is ₹0/1.3941/3.5894/5.3781/5.9578/8.2633 crore. Five-year CAGR is NM from zero; four-year startup CAGR 56.03% is disclosed but not the scoring basis. Preferred FY2023–FY2026 CAGR is 32.04%, with annual additions ₹1.7887/0.5797/2.3055 crore. FY26 H1 revenue 3.1007 and H2 revenue 5.1626 imply 40.42% and 38.08% growth against the reported half-year comparatives; no separate trajectory bonus. Prior reported half-year sales sum 1.06 lakh below the annual total; use the audited annual sequence for CAGR. Material/labour reclassifications prevent naive historical gross-margin comparisons. FY25–FY26 sales less materials rises only₹0.2600 crore despite₹2.3055 crore more sales; no verified price/volume bridge or acquisition contribution is invented. [S1–S6]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Management reports a commissioned heavy-metal line expanding capacity about 1.5 times, and in-house powder manufacture; actual utilization, tonnes coated and booked demand are not reconciled in the annual. Base 12% sales growth reaches ₹15.5580 crore annualized by October 2031. To avoid treating all expansion as free, the model assumes only 15% opening capacity headroom, then ₹1 of capital for each ₹3 additional annual sales, maintenance 1.1 times modeled depreciation, and actual opening WC. Bear/bull use 5%/30% headroom and 2x/4x incremental capital turnover. These are assumptions, not issuer forecasts. Historical FY2024–FY2026 incremental NOPAT/IC is onlyabout 0.66%; plant/land ramp lags are the counterargument, not proof of attractive cohorts. GQS 5.9 reflects growth that has not yet produced consistently strong incremental cash economics. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Jagjit Singh Dhillon combines MD/CFO roles; Navneet Kaur became whole-time director from April 2026 under the postal ballot with ₹50,000 monthly basic pay plus permitted benefits. FY26 disclosed related rent ₹0.1440 crore, machine hire ₹0.0120 crore and labour ₹0.1367 crore; director remuneration payable ₹0.2787 crore is retained as an opening cash obligation. Prospectus risk 3 disclosed promoter assets bought without a registered-valuation report and unpaid at that historical date; current annual trade/debt balances, not that old amount again, drive the model. Auditors repeated incomplete audit-trail observations inFY25/FY26; FY26 says the appointed internal auditor’s report was not supplied. May 30 company correction was confined to cash flow according to its cover letter. These are disclosed control limitations, not allegations of fraud. Capacity delivery is evidenced by management’s commissioned-line statement; improvement in internal-audit output is not evidenced merely by reappointment. [S1–S5,S8,S11] The IPO schedule originally anticipated commercial production in February 2025. The later commissioned-line description is not a precise dated commissioning/use-of-proceeds reconciliation, so the delivery lag cannot be measured reliably. [S2,S12–S14]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 revenue ₹8.2633 crore/PAT ₹1.1452 crore/CFO about ₹1.29 crore; cash PPE ₹0.7181 crore and FD transfer ₹1.6441 crore. The deposit is an asset reclassification, not unexplained lost cash. Five profitable-year CFO/PAT=0.809; latest three-year=0.624, and five-year CFO less PPE=₹-0.2553 crore. Three-year conversion after stripping FY26 FD interest falls further. Receivables ₹3.8049 crore are 46.04% of annual sales, with ₹0.9026 crore over six months; suppliers ₹0.6476 crore are 1–2 years old. Opening WC ₹2.2720 crore includes all operating advances, statutory/expense/remuneration claims and current gratuity. Gross tax ₹0.3892 crore and tax credits ₹0.2222 crore settle separately once, net ₹0.1670 crore. Legacy gratuity ₹0.0275 crore remains a terminal claim; DTA is not cash. Annual and H1/H2 PAT differ ₹0.0578 crore: our tax-sign/DTA bridge explains the arithmetic but does not purport to amend the issuer filing. Use annual totals and normalized 27% cash tax, not a fabricated quarterly/TTM series. [S1–S6]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Observed ₹96.50 implies reported P/E 11.39x and P/B 1.67x. EV/operating EBIT is 8.37x excluding FD cash access, or 7.19x crediting FD at par. Base exit 7x EBIT therefore does not require rerating. Funded bear/base/bull paths use 3%/12%/20% revenue growth, 11%/16.5%/20% EBIT margins and 5x/7x/10x exits. Terminal shares stay 0.1352 crore absent financing stress; values ₹64.76/167.71/382.48 produce −7.67%/+11.69%/+31.71% annualized returns with no dividends. First seven months April–October 2026 are estimates from the audited opening, not known cash. Current FD is unavailable during the operating forecast, then added at exit with 0–100% recovery sensitivities; debt and long gratuity are deducted, only excess cash added, and WC/PPE are not liquidated a second time. Base 15% hurdle price ₹83.38 is conditional, not an executable target; same margin/exit requires 17.24% sales CAGR at current price. No IRR is assigned to an unfunded path. [S1,S5,S7,S9] The IPO prospectus earmarked ₹1.4516 crore for plant. Inspected utilization tables continue to show zero for that object, while the annual describes commissioned capacity; a current reconciliation is absent. Accordingly ₹1.4516 crore is conservatively reserved against terminal FD value, not described as an established cash payable. Removing that reserve after verified utilization/release raises the base IRR to 13.08%; it does not reach the 15% hurdle. No earmarked deposit is spent on unrelated claims. [S12–S14]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Critical variable is collection of profitable revenue without relying on overdue supplier finance. Loss of a concentrated customer can depress utilization/margin and delay receivables simultaneously. Restrained survival tests 20% revenue decline, 11% EBIT margin, 25% loss on known over-six-month receivables and repayment of all aged suppliers within six months: minimum cash remains ₹0.5655 crore without new money or FD access. This supports Conditional G3, not a guaranteed pass. A remote combined 35% decline, 6% margin,full overdue loss,₹0.8 crore additional collection delay and tax-credit delay first goes cash-negative inJuly2026 in the estimated bridge. It identifies a boundary, not current default or a credible central stress. Hypothetical rescue financing charges interest, fees and dilution and is not evidence that rescue is available. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold per-share price outcomes in five years need 37.97%/58.49% annualized appreciation. The already demanding bull grows sales 20% at 20%EBIT and 10x exit, producing about 3.96 times terminal price, not 5x or 10x. At unchanged share count, growth must also fund capacity and WC; rerating is not business compounding. A 5x/10x conclusion is speculative and unsupported on current evidence.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Use the structured eight-item plan for receivable ageing, aged creditor finance, underlying EBIT, plant utilization, cash conversion, control remediation, share/proceeds changes and trading capacity. Current baselines are dated FY26/October 2026; warning thresholds prompt research, not automatic trades. September 2026 interim results are the next operating checkpoint once published, not an already-known quarter. No automatic monitoring is created.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: BQS 5.0 and IAS 4.3 classify as Weak setup / value-trap risk under the matrix, with a research-watchlist action rather than a buy/sell instruction. Not a compounder: moat, capital efficiency, cash and stewardship are below required thresholds. A price around ₹83.38 only solves the modeled 15% base return; it does not cure liquidity or financial-control caveats. Improve classification only with collected cash, returns on the enlarged operating asset base, documented control fixes and a practicable entry/exit path. All comparisons remain provisional within the unfinished universe.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary issuer annuals FY24–FY26, lead-manager prospectus, revised signed results, half-year results, postal/AGM material and the current issuer index were read. Relocated historical files resolve the earlier retrieval gap; no old missing-history conclusion is carried forward. Financial-statement scanned tables were visually checked. BSE primary market data were unavailable; secondary dated trade observations support bounded L1, not a live quote. Outstanding gaps: current customer mix/utilization, FD maturity/lien and IPO earmarking reconciliation, exact unconfirmed balances, present internal-audit output, tax-sign clarification and live BSE depth/surveillance. FD is excluded from operating financing, so its restrictions cannot create phantom funding. These gaps remain explicit and are sensitized rather than filled with neutral scores. IPO-use tables were checked separately from their superseded or period-inconsistent financial rows. The current capital-object allocation is conservatively reserved in valuation; no allegation of diversion is made. [S12–S15]
